messages.text: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at Cheltenham

metadata.summary: Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle.
metadata.content: Cheltenham: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at November meeting | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cheltenham: Pioneer Pete sparks jubilant Greatwood scenes at November meeting Pioneer Pete continued his ascent up the two-mile hurdling rankings when taking top honours in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle under Jonjo O'Neill Jr; Tennessee Tango was second, with Morning Mayhem third. Sunday 15 November 2026 16:52, UK Image: Jonjo O'Neill Jr celebrates aboard Pioneer Pete Pioneer Pete could have the County Hurdle back at Cheltenham in March as a target after continuing his charge up the two-mile hurdling rankings in the Unibet Greatwood Handicap Hurdle. Posting a fourth win on the spin and backing up his impressive Welsh Champion Hurdle win at Chepstow, the likeable five-year-old was always in the front rank under Jonjo O'Neill Jnr and came clear to win by six and a half lengths at 7-2 from Tennessee Tango. Victory for O'Neill, winning on the horse for the fifth time and riding for his father-brother training combination of Jonjo and AJ O'Neill, put welcome gloss on a day in which he had fallen twice from three previous rides. "I thought Chepstow was his limit, but he is an amazing little horse," said O'Neill senior. "I have no idea how much more is left in the locker, but he is a horse in form and you would have to look at all those options like the County Hurdle now." messages.text: One for the World Cup? England's new-ball switch to Baker pays dividends

metadata.summary: As England impressively levelled their three-match ODI series against Australia with a 135-run win in Adelaide, might they have stumbled upon the perfect bowling formula with one eye on the 2027 Cricket World Cup?
metadata.content: England beat Australia in second ODI: Sonny Baker new-ball switch from Jofra Archer pays off in Adelaide | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis England beat Australia in second ODI: Sonny Baker new-ball switch from Jofra Archer pays off in Adelaide Gus Atkinson (4-28) and Sonny Baker (1-45) reduce Australia to 29-4 in devastating opening spell as England bounce back from Perth drubbing to level ODI series with 135-run win in Adelaide; series decider takes place in Hobart on Wednesday (play starts at 3.30am, UK time) Sunday 15 November 2026 14:17, UK Image: Sonny Baker took 1-45 in eight overs after being given the new ball by England in the second ODI win over Australia As England impressively levelled their three-match ODI series against Australia with a 135-run win in Adelaide, might they have stumbled upon the perfect bowling formula with one eye on the 2027 Cricket World Cup? Tom Banton (121 off 99 balls) was rightly named Player of the Match for his second ODI hundred that helped turn things round after a dismal defeat in Perth - from 131 all out to 355-6 in the space of 48 hours - but the bowling was equally impressive. Image: England's Tom Banton celebrates his second ODI century against Australia in Adelaide Gus Atkinson (4-28) claimed career-best ODI figures as he and Sonny Baker (1-45) helped set the tone early on by reducing Australia to 29-4 in the opening seven overs of their run-chase as they were ultimately bowled out for 220. messages.text: Australia brush off New Zealand to win fourth straight Rugby League World Cup

metadata.summary: Jack Bostock and Liam Martin both starred as Australia swept away New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final to be crowned world champions for the fourth time in a row.
metadata.content: Men's Rugby League World Cup final - Australia 32-12 New Zealand: Kangaroos brush off Kiwis to win fourth straight world title | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Men's Rugby League World Cup final - Australia 32-12 New Zealand: Kangaroos brush off Kiwis to win fourth straight world title Australia reigned supreme as they successfully defended their world title for the fourth consecutive time, as they beat New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final Sunday 15 November 2026 11:55, UK Image: Australia won their fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup after defeating New Zealand on Sunday Jack Bostock and Liam Martin both starred as Australia swept away New Zealand 32-12 in the men's Rugby League World Cup final to be crowned world champions for the fourth time in a row. Australia had begun the tournament slowly, narrowly beating New Zealand 24-22 in their World Cup curtain-raiser in October, but when it came to the business end of the World Cup, they showcased why they are the best team in the world. It ushered in another era of dominance for Australian Rugby League, after the Jillaroos also completed a four-peat of World Cup victories, following their 34-10 victory against New Zealand's women's side earlier on Sunday. New Zealand had been out to win their first World Cup since 2008, but James Fisher-Harris' side were errant in defence, missing 37 tackles as Reece Walsh and Bradman Best tore apart the Kiwi line. messages.text: Zverev begins ATP Finals with straight sets victory over Jodar

metadata.summary: Alexander Zverev began his ATP Finals campaign with a 6-4 6-4 victory over rising star Rafael Jodar, who was competing in the event for the first time.
metadata.content: ATP Finals: World No 1 Alexander Zverev begins campaign with convincing straight-sets victory over Rafael Jodar | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content ATP Finals: World No 1 Alexander Zverev begins campaign with convincing straight-sets victory over Rafael Jodar Alexander Zverev beat Spain's Rafael Jodar 6-4 6-4 as the ATP Finals begins in Turin; Jodar is the first man to qualify for the Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut; You can watch the Nitto ATP Finals from November 15-22 in Turin on Sky Sports Tennis Sunday 15 November 2026 16:55, UK Image: Germany's Alexander Zverev returns the ball to Spain's Rafael Jodar. (AP Photo/Luca Bruno) Alexander Zverev began his ATP Finals campaign with a 6-4 6-4 victory over rising star Rafael Jodar, who was competing in the event for the first time. Zverev claimed his first two Grand Slam titles this year and became world No 1 for the first time too. He is aiming for his third ATP Finals trophy after taking the season-ending event in 2018 and 2021. "It's been a very good year for me. A lot of things that I've wanted to achieve I have achieved this year," Zverev said. "But playing here you can never take it for granted." The 20-year-old Jodar is the first man to qualify for the Finals in the same season as his tour-level debut.
